scenarios.title: A short guessing game
scenarios.task: Arrange a short Twenty Questions-style game for a fictional cognitive activity. You choose an everyday object in secret. Agree who asks, answers and guesses, what answers are allowed, the limit, and how to stop. Use your own words; you may negotiate a supported alternative. Keep your camera on during the interaction. Facial-expression estimates are fallible observations, not answers to the game.
scenarios.privatePrompt: Privately record the object and one preference for the activity. Do not reveal the object to the assistant.

revision.prompt: Ask to change the question limit to three in total, including questions already asked, keeping the roles and other agreed requirements unchanged. Record your prediction, then review and accept the revised proposal.

probe.prompt: During the game, ask to pause, then explicitly resume when ready.

understanding.prompt: Who knows the secret, who asks the questions, and who guesses?
What will happen when the agreed question limit is reached?
What changed in the revised agreement, and which earlier requirements still applied? If no revision was accepted, select Not applicable.

rubric: Secret ownership and roles faithfully agreed
Answer types and question/guess budget explicit
Pause preserves the game; budget exhaustion is not success

scenarios.title: A fictional routine check-in
scenarios.task: Arrange a fictional medication-routine check-in. Agree when it may begin, how to respond if the fictional routine is not completed, what to do when more people are visible, and what departure or return means. Do not provide personal medical information. Use a camera and arrange a consenting adult helper who can briefly enter and leave its view. Explain that person-count and facial-expression estimates will be transmitted and stored, but camera images and audio will not. Use fictional information only. If a helper is unavailable, finish with a technical problem rather than simulate their presence.
scenarios.privatePrompt: Privately record one preference for supportive wording and one condition under which you want the check-in postponed.

revision.prompt: Ask for shorter, neutral support wording while preserving all agreed context and stopping conditions.

probe.prompt: After the first check-in question, and before answering, ask your consenting helper to enter the camera view beside you, then leave while you remain visible. Observe the detected count and the response. Once one person is visible again, explicitly resume. Do not leave the view yourself until this probe is complete.

understanding.prompt: What should happen when two people are visible?
What permits the check-in to resume after postponement?
What changed in the revised agreement, and which earlier requirements still applied? If no revision was accepted, select Not applicable.

rubric: Observable conditions explicitly agreed without identity claims
Absence, stale evidence, and completion remain distinct

scenarios.title: Agreeing on answer signs
scenarios.task: Arrange a short fictional check-in using real hand signs in your camera view. Negotiate thumbs-up and thumbs-down as answers and open palm as wait. Agree which question a sign answers, how to resume, and how to finish. Lower your hand between signs; a held sign counts only once. Demonstrations do not accept a proposal.
scenarios.privatePrompt: Privately record your preferred yes/no mapping and one requirement for waiting or resuming.

revision.prompt: Request the opposite yes/no mapping, preserving the agreed wait and stopping rules. Review and accept the change.

probe.prompt: Use open palm while a question is pending, then resume according to your agreement and answer it.

understanding.prompt: Which sign currently means yes, and which means no?
What happens to the pending question when you signal wait?
What changed in the revised agreement, and which earlier requirements still applied? If no revision was accepted, select Not applicable.

rubric: Mappings and their scope explicitly agreed
One sign answers one pending question
Revised mapping needs acceptance and does not reinterpret prior answers

pre.prompt: How often have you used a conversational AI system?
What experience have you had interacting with robots?
Have you used PROMETHEUS before? If so, briefly describe how.
I am comfortable completing this activity in English.

post.prompt: This system's capabilities meet my requirements.
This system is easy to use.
The agreement was clear to me.
I could correct the assistant's misunderstandings.
I could control changes to the agreed activity.
Establishing and revising the agreement required a lot of effort.
What, if anything, did the assistant misunderstand?
Describe a moment when its behavior differed from your expectations, if any.

debrief: This study examines how people establish, understand and revise agreements with an assistant. Typed conversation is combined with browser-based estimates of facial expression, visible-person count and hand signs. Recognition can be wrong: an expression is not a reliable measure of feelings, a count does not establish identity or privacy, and recorded answers do not establish clinical outcomes. No camera images or microphone audio are uploaded or stored by this application. The server stores derived observations, conversation, agreements and your separate study answers. This is not healthcare or a physical robot trial. Your answers are now locked; the study receipt identifies this attempt.
